synthesis.headline: 14% of low-tech-comfort residents cannot identify if their block is affected — the single biggest barrier to compliance.

findings.claim: 96% of low-tech-comfort residents (tech_comfort ≤ 30) cite inability to identify affected blocks as their top confusion.
78% of high-skepticism residents (skepticism ≥ 70) cite hidden or extra permit fees as their top objection.
70% of low-income residents (income_band <25k) cite cost as top objection and demand income-based fee waivers.

highest_leverage_edit.current_text: Residents who are unsure whether their specific block falls within a newly designated zone should consult the zone map published on the Department of Transportation's website or contact the Parking Services Division directly.
highest_leverage_edit.proposed_text: Residents can verify their exact block status instantly at riverton.gov/zone-check or by texting 'ZONE' to 555-0199.
highest_leverage_edit.rationale: Replaces vague direction with direct link and SMS shortcut; 45 personas explicitly request exact block lookup or map link in what_would_change_my_mind.

synthesis.who_you_are_losing: Low-tech-comfort, high-skepticism Riverton residents in expansion zones who cannot verify block inclusion or afford undisclosed permit fees.
synthesis.who_you_are_winning: High-tech-comfort, low-skepticism residents who routinely use city portals and treat permit costs as negligible overhead.
